newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL CONGRESS WEEK-Lawmakers take a breather.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL CONGRESS WEEK-Lawmakers take a breather.

text.p: The normally bustling corridors of Brazil's Congress were likely to be empty and silent this week as lawmakers stayed in their home states for a week-long break, officials said Monday.
"There's absolutely no one here and there won't be until next week," a congressional aide said. A Senate official said there would no activity in the upper house either.

The month of July is normally a recess for Brazil's deputies and senators. But this year the government called an extraordinary session of Congress through July 25 in the hope of making up for time lost on key pieces of legislation.
Government whips, seeking to justify triple salaries of about $23,000 lawmakers earned for their labors in July, hailed the extraordinary session as a success.
In interviews with newspapers, they cited first round votes on a civil service reform bill and another bill extending the government's Fiscal Stabilization Fund as important victories.
However, many political observers noted the government failed to meet hopes that those bills would be put to both their lower house votes during the extraordinary session and advance to the Senate.
The government also did not manage to hold a first full Senate vote on its long-suffering pension reform bill which was only approved in an upper house committee last week.
